subject.title: [Feature]: Inline agent widgets in web chat via client-capability-gated tools

question: Should OpenClaw accept a generic `requiredClientCaps` tool contract plus a Canvas-owned `show_widget` web-chat widget surface, or narrow/defer the API before shipping inline widgets?
rationale: The issue is a feature/API request that changes plugin-visible tool availability and model-authored markup rendering policy; automation cannot choose that durable product and security boundary on its own.

options.title: Accept after PR repair
options.body: Use the linked PR as the implementation path once its gates are repaired and the sandbox/API contract is explicitly accepted.

options.title: Narrow the API first
options.body: Keep the widget goal but redesign or hide the capability contract until maintainers are ready to expose a plugin-visible availability seam.

options.title: Defer bundled widgets
options.body: Leave the issue open but unscheduled or move experimentation outside core until stronger product demand and security posture are proven.

recommendation.title: Accept after PR repair
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR as the implementation path once its gates are repaired and the sandbox/API contract is explicitly accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current proposal and open implementation candidate and is the strongest current routing signal for the product/API decision.
